details.history: Founded in the 7th century as Gion-sha, the shrine became the cult center of the Gion faith that arose to placate epidemics. It was renamed Yasaka Shrine in 1868 during the Meiji separation of Buddhism and Shinto (shinbutsu bunri).
details.why_visit: The head shrine of roughly 2,300 Yasaka/Gion shrines nationwide and the spiritual home of the Gion Matsuri, one of Japan's three great festivals. Its vermilion West Gate above Shijo-dori is a defining Kyoto landmark.
details.prayer_focus: Protection from epidemics and misfortune (厄除け yakuyoke), prosperity in business (商売繁盛), and good fortune.
details.best_season: July for the Gion Matsuri; cherry blossoms in adjacent Maruyama Park in early April; lantern-lit evenings year-round.

deities.role: Chief enshrined deity (主祭神); protector against plague and misfortune.
deities.regional_lore: At Yasaka, Susanoo was long venerated in a fused identity with Gozu Tenno (牛頭天王), the Buddhist-derived deity of pestilence, until the 1868 separation restored his Shinto name. The Gion Matsuri originated as a goryo-e rite to appease him and quell epidemics.

canonical.domain: Storms, sea, and the slaying of Yamata-no-Orochi
canonical.canonical_lore: Born from Izanagi's nose and banished from Takamagahara, Susanoo slew the eight-headed serpent Yamata-no-Orochi and recovered the sword Kusanagi. (Kojiki / Nihon Shoki)

deities.role: Consort of Susanoo, enshrined alongside him.

canonical.canonical_lore: The maiden rescued by Susanoo from Yamata-no-Orochi and taken as his wife.

events.time_prose: Throughout July; Yamaboko Junko float processions on July 17 (Saki Matsuri) and July 24 (Ato Matsuri).
events.origin: Originated in 869 as a goryo-e rite to dispel a nationwide epidemic, sending 66 halberds to the Shinsen-en garden for the provinces of Japan.
events.meaning: A purification of the city and a petition for protection from pestilence and disaster.
events.ritual: Mikoshi processions, the towering yamaboko floats, and the Yamaboko Junko parade through central Kyoto.
events.prayer: For freedom from disease and disaster.
events.visitor_notes: The float processions on the 17th and 24th draw large crowds; arrive early along Shijo-dori.

deities.role: Honored deity carried in the mikoshi
